name: Open USD
oneLiner: OUSD is Bridge's dollar for Open Standard, backed by cash and short Treasuries, with fee-free 1:1 business minting and redemption.
collateral: Cash and short-dated U.S. Treasuries, including government money-market funds with T-bill ladders under three months. Open Standard names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY as reserve institutions; their allocation shares are not disclosed.
pegMechanism: Bridge Building Inc. issues OUSD for the Open Standard programme, natively on Tempo, Ethereum, Base and Solana. Businesses mint and redeem at a 1:1 USD conversion rate with no fees or artificial volume limits. Direct redemption requires eligibility and onboarding as a Bridge User; binding terms provide processing within two business days after compliance acceptance and give holders no property interest in reserve assets.

proofOfReserves.provider: Bridge's self-reported live reserves dashboard; Open Standard announces monthly attestations, but no independent report is published yet

notices.title: Distinct from Origin Dollar
notices.message: Open USD is issued by Bridge for Open Standard. It shares the OUSD ticker with Origin Dollar, a separate stablecoin from Origin Protocol.

milestones.title: Open Standard unveils Open USD (OUSD), a partner-governed consortium stablecoin
milestones.description: 140+ businesses back a fully-reserved dollar that shares most reserve earnings with partners, with zero mint/redeem fees and no volume limits. Circle shares fell ~15-17% on the news.

milestones.title: 140+ launch partners including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Stripe, BlackRock, Coinbase, and PayPay Corporation
Zach Abrams (Bridge co-founder) named interim CEO; Fireblocks selected for settlement; OUSD to launch natively on Solana
Open Standard CEO essay sets OUSD economics: 'incentivize utility, not AUM'
milestones.description: Zach Abrams's post described the business model: fee-free minting and redemption, a small per-transaction developer fee, and shared reserve revenue structured to reward transaction utility over assets under management. No launch date or contracts were given.

milestones.title: Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa named initial founding partners with $1B+ launch liquidity commitment
milestones.description: Open Standard named its five initial founding partners, each investing in the company and helping establish OUSD supply for more than $1 billion of near-term launch liquidity, and Zach Abrams moved from interim to full-time CEO. Open Standard publishes no contract address and the site still describes OUSD as not yet live; CoinGecko carries only a preview placeholder.

milestones.title: Open USD launches on Tempo, Ethereum, Base and Solana
milestones.description: Open Standard publishes the four official contracts and names Bridge as issuer. Businesses can mint and burn at a 1:1 USD conversion rate without fees; reserves are held at BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY. Monthly attestations are announced, with no independent report published at launch.
